title: Effects of Turbidity on the Larval Survival of the Pelagic Shrimp Lucensosergia lucens in Suruga Bay, Japan
content:
ABSTRACT

In recent years, the pelagic shrimp Lucensosergia lucens population in Suruga Bay has declined drastically. One factor contributing to these declines is the influx of turbid river water into the inner bay, which serves as a spawning ground for pelagic shrimp. Here, we investigated the effects of particle concentration and particle size on pelagic shrimp larvae, as well as the vertical distribution of particles and larvae within inner Suruga Bay. The survival rate of pelagic shrimp larvae decreased as particle concentration increased, and this effect was particularly pronounced at a particle size of 100 μm for nauplius larva and 10 μm for elaphocaris larva. Particles in the inner bay were predominantly inorganic, with a modal size of 100–200 μm. Both the particle concentration in Fuji River water and the number of high-turbidity days have increased over time. These findings suggest that inorganic particles approximately 100 μm in size, entering from the river, may negatively affect the survival of pelagic shrimp larvae.
